brief: Goldman Sachs' October PPI note: headline PPI rose 0.3% month-over-month (6.5% y/y), in line with GS's own forecast but below the 0.4% median forecast, with September's prior revised up to 1.4%. Core PPI (ex food and energy) also rose 0.3% (5.0% y/y), above GS's 0.2% forecast. PPI ex food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% (4.9% y/y), above both GS's and the median forecast. Energy prices fell 0.1%, reversing two months of sharp increases GS ties to the re-escalation of the Iran conflict. Retailer margins fell 0.2% after September's largest increase since March 2022. Core intermediate prices rose 0.9% while crude materials ex food and energy fell 0.9%, their first decline since June. The PCE-relevant PPI components (domestic airfares -1.8%, medical care services an estimated +0.14% month-over-month) came in net softer than GS expected, so GS lowered its core PCE month-over-month estimate to 0.30% from a pre-PPI 0.35%, putting core PCE at 3.24% year-over-year, and raised its headline PCE estimate to 0.32% month-over-month.
